scenes.tts: One amino acid, glycine, can carry plus one, zero, or minus one. What decides which? One comparison, made at every proton switch.
scenes.caption: One amino acid, glycine, can carry +1, 0, or −1. What decides which? One comparison, made at every proton switch.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for the whole film: proton = GOLD token; acid-type switch = ORANGE; base-type switch = BLUE; net charge = TEAL; pH cursor = WHITE. One world: a pH axis 0 to 14 runs across the bottom third of the frame with a white cursor; the amino acid sits above it as a large rounded block with switch sockets; a TEAL net-charge readout sits at the right. Opens on the world at full size, no title. A large rounded block labelled 'glycine' (fills ~60% of frame height) sits above the pH axis; on its face a big TEAL readout 'net charge'. From the first frame the white pH cursor glides slowly from pH 1 to pH 12 and back; the readout reads off a computed glycine net charge (pKa 2.34 and 9.60) and rolls +1 → 0 → −1 as the cursor passes. On 'What decides' the readout swells and a white '?' appears beside it. On 'proton switch' two empty sockets on the block (left and right) pulse once.
scenes.narration: One amino acid, glycine, can carry +1, 0, or −1. What decides which? One comparison, made at every proton switch.

scenes.visual: Title card, 2 s: 'Add Up the Proton Switches'. The glycine block stays faintly behind it with the cursor still drifting.

scenes.tts: A proton switch is a group that holds a hydrogen ion, a proton, or lets it go. Holding it is protonated. Letting go is deprotonated.
scenes.visual: Camera zooms into the left socket until one switch fills the frame: a big toggle lever on a base plate. A GOLD token labelled 'H+' sits in a cup at the lever's tip and bobs gently. On 'holds' the cup closes round the token; on 'lets it go' the cup opens and the token floats up and away. On 'protonated' the token drifts back in and the label 'protonated' writes under the lever; on 'deprotonated' the token lifts off again and the label morphs into 'deprotonated'. Faint specks drift in the background throughout.
scenes.narration: A proton switch is a group that holds a hydrogen ion, a proton, or lets it go. Holding it is protonated. Letting go is deprotonated.

scenes.tts: Each switch has a set point, its p K a. That is the p H where half the groups hold a proton. Below it, most hold on. Above it, most let go.
scenes.caption: Each switch has a set point, its pKa. That is the pH where half the groups hold a proton. Below it, most hold on. Above it, most let go.
scenes.visual: The single switch shrinks and copies itself into a grid of 20 small identical switches above the pH axis. A vertical dashed line rises from the axis at pH 4, labelled 'pKa (example)'. On 'set point' the line pulses. On 'half the groups' the cursor sits on the line, exactly 10 of 20 switches hold a GOLD token, and a bar gauge at right reads 'holding H+: 50%'. On 'Below it' the cursor slides to pH 3 and tokens drop back in until the computed share is held (1/(1+10^(pH−pKa)), about 18 of 20); on 'Above it' it slides to pH 5 and tokens fly off until about 2 of 20 hold. Tokens keep bobbing in their cups.
scenes.narration: Each switch has a set point, its pKa. That is the pH where half the groups hold a proton. Below it, most hold on. Above it, most let go.

scenes.tts: Each p H unit from the p K a changes the ratio of the two forms tenfold. One unit above, about ninety-one percent have let go.
scenes.caption: Each pH unit from the pKa changes the ratio of the two forms tenfold. One unit above, about 91% have let go.
scenes.visual: Same grid and gauge; the cursor returns to the pKa line. Tick marks at 'pKa' and 'pKa + 1' appear on the axis, and a ratio readout 'let go : hold' over '1 : 1' sits beside the gauge. On 'tenfold' the cursor glides one unit right while the ratio counts up to '10 : 1'. On 'ninety-one percent' the gauge (computed, tagged 'computed') fills to 'let go: 91%' and tokens leave the grid until 18 of 20 are empty.
scenes.narration: Each pH unit from the pKa changes the ratio of the two forms tenfold. One unit above, about 91% have let go.

scenes.tts: A proton carries plus one, so holding it makes a group one charge more positive. An acid-type switch, like a carboxyl, goes from zero to minus one. A base-type switch, like an amino group, goes from plus one to zero. So letting go is not always negative.
scenes.caption: A proton carries +1, so holding it makes a group one charge more positive. An acid-type switch, like a carboxyl, goes from 0 to −1. A base-type switch, like an amino group, goes from +1 to 0. So letting go is not always negative.
scenes.visual: The grid collapses into two large switches side by side, each filling half the frame. A '+1' tag rides on each GOLD token. On 'acid-type' the left switch turns ORANGE, labelled 'acid type (carboxyl)', charge badge '0'; its token leaves and the badge morphs to '−1'. On 'base-type' the right switch turns BLUE, labelled 'base type (amino)', badge '+1'; its token leaves and the badge morphs to '0'. On 'not always negative' the BLUE badge '0' pulses and a line writes under it: 'let go = neutral'.
scenes.narration: A proton carries +1, so holding it makes a group one charge more positive. An acid-type switch, like a carboxyl, goes from 0 to −1. A base-type switch, like an amino group, goes from +1 to 0. So letting go is not always negative.

scenes.tts: Glycine has two backbone switches. The carboxyl's p K a is about two point three; the amino group's, about nine point six. Here is the whole idea: net charge is the sum of the switches.
scenes.caption: Glycine has two backbone switches. The carboxyl's pKa is about 2.3; the amino group's, about 9.6. Here is the whole idea: net charge is the sum of the switches.
scenes.visual: The two switches slide into the left and right sockets of the 'glycine' block from the hook, which settles back above the pH axis. On 'carboxyl's' an ORANGE dashed pKa line rises from the axis at 2.34, labelled 'pKa 2.3'; on 'amino group's' a BLUE dashed line rises at 9.60, labelled 'pKa 9.6'. On 'sum of the switches' each switch's badge slides along an arrow into the TEAL readout, which shows '(badge) + (badge) = net'. The cursor waits at the left end.
scenes.narration: Glycine has two backbone switches. The carboxyl's pKa is about 2.3; the amino group's, about 9.6. Here is the whole idea: net charge is the sum of the switches.

scenes.tts: Your turn. At blood p H, about seven point four, check each switch against its p K a. What is glycine's net charge?
scenes.caption: Your turn. At blood pH, about 7.4, check each switch against its pKa. What is glycine's net charge?
scenes.visual: The white cursor slides to pH 7.4 and a label 'blood, about 7.4' appears above it. Both switches' badges turn into '?', and their GOLD tokens hover above the cups. On 'net charge' a question card writes across the top: 'Glycine at pH 7.4: net charge?'
scenes.narration: Your turn. At blood pH, about 7.4, check each switch against its pKa. What is glycine's net charge?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause: the question card stays; the two '?' badges pulse slowly; the GOLD tokens hover, undecided. Background specks keep drifting.

scenes.tts: Seven point four is above the carboxyl's p K a, so it lets go: minus one. It is below the amino group's, so it holds on: plus one. The sum is zero: a zwitterion, with both a plus and a minus.
scenes.caption: 7.4 is above the carboxyl's pKa, so it lets go: −1. It is below the amino group's, so it holds on: +1. The sum is zero: a zwitterion, with both a plus and a minus.
scenes.visual: The question card fades. On 'above the carboxyl's' an arrow shows the cursor right of the ORANGE line; the ORANGE token flies off and its badge becomes '−1'. On 'below the amino group's' an arrow shows the cursor left of the BLUE line; the BLUE token drops into its cup and the badge becomes '+1'. On 'The sum is zero' both badges slide into the TEAL readout: '−1 + +1 = 0'. On 'zwitterion' the block outline glows, a small '+' and '−' light at the two sockets, and the label 'zwitterion' writes beneath.
scenes.narration: 7.4 is above the carboxyl's pKa, so it lets go: −1. It is below the amino group's, so it holds on: +1. The sum is zero: a zwitterion, with both a plus and a minus.

scenes.tts: Sweep the p H upward, and the predominant charge steps down: plus one, zero, minus one. Each drop is centred on a p K a. The exact zero crossing is the isoelectric point, the p I.
scenes.caption: Sweep the pH upward, and the predominant charge steps down: +1, 0, −1. Each drop is centred on a pKa. The exact zero crossing is the isoelectric point, the pI.
scenes.visual: The block shrinks to the upper left; a TEAL plot grows above the pH axis: average net charge (−1 to +1) against pH, tagged 'computed'. On 'Sweep' the cursor travels 0 → 14 and the continuous curve is drawn behind it, computed from the two switches (pKa 2.34 and 9.60); the switches on the small block flip in sync. On 'steps down' the three near-plateaus glow and get labels 'about +1', 'about 0', 'about −1'. On 'centred on' the ORANGE and BLUE dashed lines reach up through the middle of each curved drop. On 'zero crossing' a TEAL dot appears at the curve's unique zero crossing; label 'pI'.
scenes.narration: Sweep the pH upward, and the predominant charge steps down: +1, 0, −1. Each drop is centred on a pKa. The exact zero crossing is the isoelectric point, the pI.

scenes.tts: For glycine, averaging its two p K a values gives the p I, about five point nine seven. In its simplest form, average the two p K a values around the ladder's net-zero rung.
scenes.caption: For glycine, averaging its two pKa values gives the pI, about 5.97. In its simplest form, average the two pKa values around the ladder's net-zero rung.
scenes.visual: On 'average' the labels '2.34' and '9.60' lift off their lines, slide together and merge into '5.97' over the TEAL pI dot. On 'ladder's' the curve's three near-plateaus swing upright into a ladder of three rungs, '+1' top, '0' middle, '−1' bottom, tagged 'predominant charge (schematic)', with '2.34' (ORANGE) and '9.60' (BLUE) written in the gaps between rungs. On 'zero rung' the middle rung glows TEAL and two brackets close from the pKa labels just above and below it.
scenes.narration: For glycine, averaging its two pKa values gives the pI, about 5.97. In its simplest form, average the two pKa values around the ladder's net-zero rung.

scenes.tts: A side chain adds a third switch, or none. Glutamate's acid switch, near four, has let go at blood p H: negative. Lysine's base switch, near ten and a half, holds on: positive. Histidine's, near six, is mostly neutral. Inside a protein, neighbours can shift these values.
scenes.caption: A side chain adds a third switch, or none. Glutamate's acid switch, near 4, has let go at blood pH: negative. Lysine's base switch, near 10.5, holds on: positive. Histidine's, near 6, is mostly neutral. Inside a protein, neighbours can shift these values.
scenes.visual: The ladder folds back into the block, which grows a third socket on top labelled 'side chain'; cursor parked at 7.4. On 'Glutamate's' the block's label morphs to 'glutamate' and an ORANGE switch snaps into the top socket with a pKa line near 4; its token flies off and its badge reads '−1'. On 'Lysine's' the label morphs to 'lysine' and a BLUE switch swaps in with a pKa line near 10.5; its token drops in, badge '+1'. On 'Histidine's' the label morphs to 'histidine', BLUE switch with a pKa line at 6, token off, badge '0' with a small tag 'mostly'. On 'Inside a protein' a soft outline labelled 'protein (schematic)' wraps round the block and the BLUE pKa line slides slowly rightward, labelled 'can shift'.
scenes.narration: A side chain adds a third switch, or none. Glutamate's acid switch, near 4, has let go at blood pH: negative. Lysine's base switch, near 10.5, holds on: positive. Histidine's, near 6, is mostly neutral. Inside a protein, neighbours can shift these values.

scenes.tts: So list the switches, compare each p K a with the p H, and add. That sum is how sickle cell hemoglobin was first told apart. A valine had replaced a glutamate on each beta chain.
scenes.caption: So list the switches, compare each pKa with the pH, and add. That sum is how sickle-cell hemoglobin was first told apart. A valine had replaced a glutamate on each beta chain.
scenes.visual: The protein outline fades. Three beats on the block: on 'list' its switches light up one by one; on 'compare' each pKa line flashes against the cursor; on 'add' the badges slide into the TEAL readout. On 'sickle cell' the block morphs into two schematic blobs, 'normal hemoglobin' and 'sickle hemoglobin', on a horizontal strip with '−' at the left end and '+' at the right, tagged 'schematic'. On 'A valine' two ORANGE switches drop out of the sickle blob and plain chips 'Val (no switch)' take their places; its TEAL readout steps two units more positive. On 'beta chain' both blobs slide toward '+', the sickle one lagging behind.
scenes.narration: So list the switches, compare each pKa with the pH, and add. That sum is how sickle-cell hemoglobin was first told apart. A valine had replaced a glutamate on each beta chain.

scenes.visual: End card: 'Net charge is the sum of switches: pH against each pKa.' The two hemoglobin blobs fade behind it; one GOLD token drifts slowly across.
